name: Museum Tiroler Bauernhöfe
kurzbeschreibung: Museum of Tyrolean Farmhouses in Kramsach: Tyrol's largest open-air museum with 14 original farmhouses and 37 outbuildings from all parts of the region, spread over 8 hectares.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Museum of Tyrolean Farmhouses in Kramsach, in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley, is the largest open-air museum in Tyrol. Nestled in a picturesque hilly landscape near the Kramsach lakes, spread over eight hectares of open-air grounds, the museum takes its guests on a vivid journey back in time to the rural past. 14 original farmhouses and 37 historic outbuildings from various valleys of North, South, and East Tyrol have been saved from decay and meticulously rebuilt here. The open-air museum offers authentic insights into the arduous life and work of Tyrolean mountain farmers in past centuries, shaped by the rhythm of nature.

Route & Requirements

The initiative for its founding came from the dedicated Kramsach teacher and local historian Heinz Mantl (1921–2014), who recognized the impending loss of historical timber architecture due to modernization in the 1970s. In 1974, the museum association was founded, and the official opening took place in 1977. Each individual building was carefully documented beam by beam at its original location in the Tyrolean valleys, dismantled, and faithfully re-erected on the museum grounds.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum of Tyrolean Farmhouses is open seasonally from Palm Sunday/end of March to the end of October daily. Opening hours: In mid-summer (May to September) daily from 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM (last admission 4:30 PM); in the pre- and post-season (March/April and October) daily from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM (last admission 3:30 PM). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Adults €13.00, children and teenagers from 6 to 17 years €5.00, children under 6 years free; family ticket (2 adults + own children) €26.00. With the regional Alpbachtal Card, admission is free. Arrival by train: ÖBB to Brixlegg station, from there take VVT bus line 601 or 611 directly to the Kramsach Abzw. Tiroler Bauernhöfe stop (approx. three minutes walk from there).

Tips

The approximately three-kilometer-long circular path leads over natural gravel and dirt paths through gently rolling meadow terrain; for wheelchairs and standard strollers, an all-terrain model or strong pushing assistance is recommended (the historical wooden parlors have high door sills due to their construction). A disabled-accessible toilet is available in the modern entrance building. For children, there is an exciting riddle rally at the ticket counter. Stop at the historic Rohrerhof from 1581 directly on the museum grounds and enjoy traditional Tyrolean Kasspatzln or Kaiserschmarrn in the beer garden. The museum also regularly offers special events and craft demonstrations that make the visit even more lively.
